title: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire
subtitle: A Poké Ball takes the place of the ball

body: Pokémon Pinball: Ruby & Sapphire is Jupiter's Game Boy Advance pinball game adapting the creatures and world of Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire into two themed tables. Keeping the ball in play produces points, while special modes turn successful shots into attempts to catch and evolve Pokémon. The collection gives the score chase another continuing purpose, with a Pokédex recording the creatures obtained across sessions. Familiar characters become parts of the table's machinery and targets, making the pinball layout another way of exploring a region already associated with travelling and collecting companions.

Catching a Pokémon is connected with activating a mode and completing its objectives while continuing to control the ball. The player has to direct shots toward useful targets without losing the basic rhythm of keeping the ball above the flippers. The two tables provide different arrangements and available encounters, giving the choice of table a consequence beyond its appearance. A successful catch therefore becomes a small sequence inside the larger run, asking for focused control at the moment when the opportunity to add another creature has finally been made available.

The Pokédex provides a record that lasts beyond an individual score attempt, allowing a shorter session to achieve something through a new catch or evolution. Bonus challenges vary the action between periods on the main table. The combination gives different players different reasons to continue: a high score can remain the immediate aim, while the collection supplies a longer project assembled through repeated encounters. Ruby & Sapphire retains the recognisable skill of pinball, but gives its targets identities that make a particular successful shot memorable after the ball has finally been lost.
